scope: First ordinary before-call matrix and only the shared inactive fault/flow helpers it needs. No original producer, compiler, native executable, helper or collector; later profile/phase, lower readback, close-error and omission domains remain separate.
prospective_resolution: CallPlan.pm builds a pure Perl call forest from each new context, original archive specification and before-release physical records. Before release, retain those inputs, the exact typed selector and resolved current call ID. The unchanged independently pinned Python flow_model.py must reconstruct the complete forest and resolution. Never select by a saved historical numeric ID.
fault_observer: A new CallFaultTrace.pm wraps only the previously selected symbols, inside the public-release wrapper after ReleaseTrace has installed its actual source/reader/handle hooks. Sealed helpers record before-call then tail-goto the original coderef. Unsealed helpers preserve void/list/scalar context and record after-call only when the original returns. No observer stack must require normal completion after an injected exception. Sealed after events are omitted; their canonical next-before selectors already cover those continuation aliases. Source returns can be observed but never faulted.
prefix: Assign current preorder IDs on before-call events and exact per-symbol occurrence counters. Record actual incoming callers and source/recheck/path/mode/limit/image/absence metadata where applicable. Preserve actual Base ReleaseTrace events and handles. The independent oracle derives the current complete healthy event skeleton, removes sealed-after observations, and verifies the prefix through the selected event followed only by allowed real cleanup and the failed public attempt. Any count, caller, resolution or trajectory mismatch is a retained first failure, never a different injected target.
fault_result: Use one exact diagnostic naming the typed address and require exactly one hit, public returned=1, attempt success=0, release=null, runtime_authorized=0 and executable=null. Derive unlink_attempted/completed and historical/latest absence from the current source-flow interval oracle; require exact physical after-state equal to before minus the selected hold only when unlink actually completed. Actual observed descriptors close before return, with no observer recovery or modeled close return in this slice.
bounded_publication: Retain each completed case once in a separate immutable case JSON with exact size/hash in a small matrix manifest. Keep a bounded current/in-flight case record and the complete allocation journal before release. Do not leave completed full case bodies in ArchiveFixture's growing in-memory report: its allocation and save_result callbacks would otherwise repeatedly rewrite all earlier cases. Clear the current case only after its immutable publication is verified. The final independent auditor loads case bodies individually; report falsifiers should alter a bounded row or manifest instead of copying the whole matrix.
controls: Before new allocations, pin all source and plan inputs. Qualify the pure Perl flow/resolver against saved healthy inputs and the independent Python flow, then qualify actual direct caller rejection through the new fault wrappers. A new healthy ordinary control checks the adapter's complete no-fault flow. Execute every selected before-call case exactly once; bail on and retain the first unexpected result before any repair or rerun.
durability: Archive source pins, first-run streams/exits, allocation journal, case manifest, all original case bodies, independent audit and falsifier results. Keep shared implementation and old producer bodies unchanged unless an explicitly owned first-failure repair requires a new source applicability contract. Finish book/fact/task/history, focused checks and the staged/commit workflow before another matrix leaf.
